items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: So, that was a nice experience, playing with Louis. He's a fine man, very fine man.

ctx.x: Actually, the first time I worked with Louis, I had the misfortune to have to lay off and so he came in town with a -- and brought some of his arrangements with him from back East and he had some tunes in there like "High Society," that had famous clarinet solos in it and there's nobody around town that could play the clarinet solos to "High Society." So, they made sure that they had me playing in the band out there when Louis was there, so I could play all the clarinet parts.

So, that was a nice experience, playing with Louis. He's a fine man, very fine man. So, maybe that's one of the reasons why Les Hite sent for me in the first place, because he knew that Louis was going to be coming and needing a clarinet player. So, that's --
Did you ever work with him again after that?
